motivation: Pre-loss focal persistence history predicts exact-point Thalassia re-recording beyond generic habitat history. Test whether local source-year focal abundance contains additional recovery information beyond history and community continuity.

predictor_construction.point_visit_bb: mean numeric focal Braun-Blanquet value attached to focal occurrence(s) at the sampled point; nonnumeric Reported rows remain missing
predictor_construction.point_year_bb: mean of available numeric focal point-visit Braun-Blanquet values within the source calendar year
predictor_construction.interpretation: ordinal abundance index, not percent cover
predictor_construction.node_centering: subtract stable-node mean source-point BB across eligible recovery sequences

primary_population.sequence_rule: same frozen 259 three-year exact-point Thalassia-loss sequences
primary_population.eligibility: source point-year has numeric focal Braun-Blanquet index
primary_population.outcome: Thalassia recorded present at the same meter mark in the recovery year

primary_hypothesis.statement: Within stable transects, higher-than-usual source-point Thalassia Braun-Blanquet abundance predicts one-year re-recording after focal loss beyond local history and community-continuity state.
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for the centered source-point Braun-Blanquet coefficient > 0

secondary: source-point Braun-Blanquet median among return and non-return sequences
eligible fraction of the frozen 259 recovery sequences
same coefficient without pre-loss history control, descriptive only

interpretation.supported: Local focal abundance before loss carries recovery information beyond occupancy history and community continuity, consistent with a local state-depth/reserve signal.
interpretation.unsupported: Source-point Braun-Blanquet abundance does not add robust recovery information once local history, community state, and site identity are represented.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc exact-point predictor analysis on an already-opened recovery endpoint.
Braun-Blanquet is an ordinal abundance index, not percent cover or direct biomass.
A positive result would not prove carbohydrate reserve, below-ground biomass, or demographic vigor.
Return is recorded reappearance, not genet-level recolonization.
Do not change the point-year BB aggregation, history control, node-centering, model, minima, or support threshold after opening the abundance-recovery result.
